title: Sharp hypercontractivity for finite laws
statement: Let $(\\Omega,\\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ be measurable with mean zero. Suppose $q>2$, $0<\\lambda<1/2$, and there is a finite set supporting $X$ almost surely such that each of its points has probability at least $\\lambda$. Set $\\rho=\\sqrt{\\sinh(u/q)/\\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$, where $u=\\log((1-\\lambda)/\\lambda)$. Then for every $a,b\\in\\mathbb R$, the $L^q$ norm of $a+\\rho bX$ is at most the $L^2$ norm of $a+bX$, and the $L^2$ norm of $a+\\rho bX$ is at most the $L^{q/(q-1)}$ norm of $a+bX$; in both cases $X$ belongs to the output exponent's $L^p$ space, and the exponents satisfy $1\\le p\\le q$ with $0\\le\\rho<1$.
hypotheses_covered: Each point in the finite support has probability at least $\\lambda$
replaced: Let $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $X$ be measurable and centered on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose atoms each have probability at least $\lambda$. Both $H_{2,q,\rho_*}(X)$ and $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho_*}(X)$ hold. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
